patch.value: Release verification shares the build job's timeout and waits fifteen minutes while npm's publish-time scan can hold a version longer: 2026.11.8 was published but the job was cancelled before acceptance

## Observed
On 2026-11-08 the blocker-retry Auto Release run 42451940007 cut tag v2026.11.8. Its tag-push Release run 42454411958 published @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.8 at 07:11:28Z: npm printed "+ @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.8" and "Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available".

The registry still answered E404 for the exact version at 07:31Z. The "Verify published package on npm, npx, and bunx" step had polled 59 of its 60 attempts when the "Build, Test, Publish" job hit its 60-minute timeout at 07:26Z and was cancelled. The pre-publish stages took 45 minutes that day (the coverage gate alone took 24 minutes, against 14 minutes on 2026-11-07), so the verify step got only 15 of its declared 20 minutes.

Registry acceptance and GitHub Release advertisement were skipped, and npm latest stayed at 2026.11.7. The auto-release run recorded release-workflow as its failing stage on blocker issue 1686.

## Cause
1. npm now scans every new version for malware at publish time, before the version becomes installable (GitHub changelog 2026-07-28). The scan typically takes about five minutes, and "up to 15 minutes or more" at peak times or depending on content and size. 2026.11.7 became visible 5m12s after publish (04:39:25Z to 04:44:37Z); 2026.11.8 took longer than 20 minutes. pm-wzmbvn fitted the 60-poll ceiling to the 6-8 minute propagation lag measured in 2026-09.
2. The verify step runs in the same job as build, tests and gates. Its wait budget is therefore whatever the job timeout leaves after a pre-publish phase of variable length, and nothing guarantees it the 20 minutes its step timeout declares.
3. Recovery is expensive. Re-running the failed job repeats 45 minutes of build, test and gates before it reaches a version that is already published.

## Fix direction
- Move post-publish verification into its own publication job that needs the release job and has its own timeout. That covers the npm/npx/bunx verifier, the installed agent sessions and the previous-release control selection.
- Raise the default npm metadata wait to about thirty minutes.
- Make the failure text name npm's publish-time scan and the cheap recovery: re-run only the failed publication job.
- Re-budget the Auto Release parent for the extra serial job, using the reserve formula from pm-29bwud.

## Non-goals
- No change to npm publish, trusted publishing or the immutable-tag rules.
- No retry of npm publish; publication was correct.

value.text: Codex review of PR 1687 (P2, fixed): the first cut of the publication job checked out dispatch-time main on workflow_dispatch. Exact-tag recovery of an unpublished tag publishes from the tag, so the verifiers would have read a different package.json identity and bin contract than the one published; legacy tag v2026.8.5 lacks pm-mcp-http, for example. The release job now records the published source (git rev-parse after source selection, immediately before Publish to npm) as the source_sha output, and the publication job checks out that commit. The previous-release selector comes from a sparse checkout of the reviewed dispatch source, as before. registry-acceptance-workflow.spec.ts pins the order and wiring.

value.text: Measured: @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.8 became visible on the registry at 08:06:50Z, 55m22s after Publish to npm finished at 07:11:28Z (registry time field; anonymous no-cache probes every 45-60 s returned E404 until then). 2026.11.7 took 5m12s. The first cut of this fix waited about thirty minutes, which today's hold would still have exhausted, so the default is now 360 polls (about ninety minutes): verify step 95 minutes, publication job 110, Auto Release parent 290 (cap 300, inside the 360-minute hosted job limit). Runner minutes are free for this public repository, so the longer wait costs nothing but runner occupancy. Release run 42454411958 was re-run with --failed at 08:08Z; Publish to npm skips because the version is visible.

value.text: Codex review round 7 of PR 1687 (P1, fixed). tests/integration/release-automation-contract.spec.ts still pinned the verify command without --npm-attempts 360. The release workflow runs that spec in its mandatory coverage gate, so the next tag release would have failed before Publish to npm. The pin now includes the explicit wait. All 8 specs that read release.yml or auto-release.yml pass (134 tests).
